reason: The quote states the default retention period configured for Enhanced Monitoring in CloudWatch Logs is 30 days; the default qualifier matches.
The quote says that after you turn it on and set a granularity, Enhanced Monitoring collects vital operating system metrics and process information at the defined granularity.

The quote supports that existing code, applications and tools should work seamlessly with RDS, but the claim's reason and engine list (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, Db2) come only from the unquoted sentence before it ('This means' refers back to it).
The quotes give free backup storage up to the account's total provisioned database storage across the region, and say it is account-specific and region-specific.
The quote supports the 3 IOPS/GB baseline and burst up to 3,000 IOPS, but 'for moderate I/O workloads' comes only from the unquoted sentence before it.
The quote says all Amazon RDS database engines are HIPAA-eligible and can store PHI under an executed BAA with AWS.

The quotes support referencing RDS resources in IAM policies and tag-based permissions, but the listed resource types (DB instances, snapshots, read replicas, parameter groups) come only from the unquoted sentence between them.
The quotes show the RDS console action 'Set up Lambda connection' for an RDS or Aurora database and the sentence 'We recommend that you use RDS Proxy during this connection set up.'
The quote states verbatim that magnetic storage is not recommended for production database instances.
The quote lists scale compute operations (generally a few minutes), engine version upgrades and required software patching as the events that take the DB instance offline.
The quote says a 30-minute default value is assigned when no preferred weekly maintenance window is specified at creation.
The quote states the window controls when modifications, engine upgrades and patching occur, and a scheduled event is initiated during the window you identify.
The quote gives a minimum six (6) month period after a major version deprecation announcement for you to initiate an upgrade.
The quote says major version upgrades will not occur automatically and must be initiated by you, except for major version deprecation.
The quote gives a three (3) month period after a minor version deprecation announcement before automatic upgrades begin.
The two quotes give the Multi-AZ recommendation for write availability and the read replica write-after-source behavior with lag that can vary significantly.
The quote covers automatic failover during certain planned maintenance or instance or AZ failure, and resumption without manual intervention because the name record stays the same.
The quote says backup storage usage does not change between standard and Multi-AZ, and backups are taken from the standby.
The quote says there should be no downtime when converting from Single-AZ to Multi-AZ, with possible increased latency while the standby catches up.
The quote says you may observe elevated latencies relative to a single-AZ deployment because of synchronous replication.
The quotes state RDS emits a DB instance event on automatic failover and that RDS Event Notifications can notify you of specific DB events.
The quote defines failover from detection on the primary to resumed transactions on the standby, typically within one to two minutes.
The lead-in quote and the four heading-scoped list lines give exactly the four automatic failover triggers in the claim.
The quote states you are not charged for data transfer incurred in replicating data between primary and standby.
Under the heading on forced failover, the quote says RDS provides an option to initiate a failover when rebooting your instance.
The quote states verbatim that running as Multi-AZ can further reduce the impact of a maintenance event.
The quote supports synchronous replication with writes concurrent on primary and standby, but 'which protects the latest updates in a failover' comes only from the next, unquoted sentence.
The quote says a Multi-AZ standby cannot serve read requests and Multi-AZ is for availability and durability rather than read scaling.
The quote states RDS automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone.
The RDS Proxy page quote states support for Multi-AZ with two readable standbys for typically under 35 second failovers, added read capacity and minor upgrade downtime typically under 1 second.
The quote says internet access must be intentionally turned on by configuring Security Groups and can be limited to specific IPs, IP ranges or subnets of your data center.
The quote supports temporary objects on NVMe instance storage instead of EBS and up to 2X faster complex queries, but the MySQL and MariaDB scope comes only from the unquoted sentence before it.
The quotes give up to 2x improved write transaction throughput for RDS for MySQL and availability at no additional cost.
The list line under 'How many databases or schemas can I run within a DB instance?' states 1 database per instance and no software limit on schemas for RDS for Oracle.
The quote states up to three additional volumes of up to 64 TiB each for Oracle and SQL Server, to a maximum of 256 TiB.
The quote says a DB parameter group acts as a container for engine configuration values that can be applied to one or more DB instances.
The quote states a default DB Parameter Group is used when a DB instance is created without specifying one.
The quote states all DB instances that use a DB parameter group get all the parameter updates to that group.
The quote describes Performance Insights as a performance tuning and monitoring feature to assess database load and determine when and where to take action.
The quote states verbatim that Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage is optimized for I/O-intensive, transactional (OLTP) database workloads.
